sections.overview: This noctuid migrates to Britain; arrivals vary greatly by year. The Belgian catalogue also describes it as a rare migrant there.
sections.identification: The adult is variable in appearance; the British field account gives a wingspan of 34–42 mm.
sections.habitat: A German species account associates it with warm, dry places that have abundant herbaceous vegetation.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on several herbaceous plants, including marigolds in the genus Calendula.
sections.behavior: In Britain, the main arrival period is June to August, while large influxes do not occur every year.
sections.reproduction: The British account notes that caterpillars are often found in good migration years, especially in southern coastal districts.
sections.ecology: Its polyphagous larvae use wild and cultivated herbaceous hosts, including garden marigolds.
sections.conservation: A Belgian catalogue calls it a rare migrant locally; this regional description is not a global threat category.
